description:
This video was made possible thanks to everyone on the Simple History Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/simplehistory

During WWII, medics used morphine via syrettes, but the transcript notes standardized dosing could be dangerous if too much was given. In the global war on terror, it says medics carried fentanyl lozenges: fentanyl absorbed through the mouth’s mucus membrane for pain relief often within about 10 minutes, with dosing easier to control because the lozenge can be removed once it takes effect. The transcript also mentions downsides—patients must be monitored for breathing issues, and medics may carry naloxone; they also need monitoring to prevent biting/swallowing the lozenge, which can increase absorption. What other battlefield pain-relief methods should we cover next?
